# Value types

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs generate` from `schemas/policy/v1.json`. Do not edit by hand. -->

Enumerations, identifiers and string formats used by the [Palisade policy document](index.md).

## AdvancedValue

A scalar value in `advanced`.

Type: boolean or integer or string.

## AllowTiebreak

Which allow decides among allows of different kinds.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `most_restrictive` | `allow_contained`, then `allow`, then `allow_elevated` (with `condition: always` before `if_required`). The default. |
| `most_permissive` | The reverse: `allow_elevated` (`if_required` before `always`), then `allow`, then `allow_contained`. |

## ApprovalScope

Who a device-local approval applies to.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `user` | Only the user who approved it. The default. |
| `device` | Every user of the device. |

## Combine

How a scope's dimensions combine.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `all` | Every dimension that is set must match. The default. |
| `any` | At least one dimension that is set must match. |

## CompliancePreset

A compliance preset: a named starting configuration. Changes that make
the policy weaker than its preset raise a compliance warning (#17).
Ordered from the least to the most demanding.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `e8_ml1` | Essential Eight maturity level 1: block in user profiles, temporary folders and other user-writable locations, detect elsewhere (ISM-1870). |
| `e8_ml2` | Essential Eight maturity level 2: block in every location (ISM-1871). |
| `e8_ml3` | Essential Eight maturity level 3: level 2, drivers blocked, and a mandatory blocklist required (ISM-1658). Drivers loaded during early boot are only audited unless `driver_boot_policy` is `enforce`; validation warns about that exemption. |

## ContainmentProfileRef

The ID of a containment profile (#14, #173).

Type: [`Uuid7`](types.md#uuid7).

## ControlLevel

Whether a class of object is controlled.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `off` | Not evaluated. |
| `audit` | Evaluated, and would-block decisions are reported only. |
| `enforce` | Evaluated and enforced. |

## Date

A calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`.

Type: string; matches `^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$`.

## DigestAlgorithm

A digest algorithm a signature uses (#31, ADR 0008).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `md2` | MD2. |
| `md5` | MD5. |
| `sha1` | SHA-1. |
| `sha256` | SHA-256. |
| `sha384` | SHA-384. |
| `sha512` | SHA-512. |

## DriverBootPolicy

How unknown drivers are handled while the device boots, before the agent
has fully started (`boot_phase: early`).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `audit` | Report what would be blocked, and block nothing. The default, until the tenant enables enforcement explicitly. |
| `enforce` | Apply the unknown-handling level. |

## ElevationAuth

The confirmation an `allow_elevated` action asks for.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `none` | No confirmation. The default. |
| `reauth` | The user authenticates again. |
| `mfa` | The user completes a multi-factor challenge. |

## ElevationCondition

When an `allow_elevated` action elevates.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `always` | Every time the object runs. |
| `if_required` | Only when the object asks for administrator rights. |

## EnforcementOverride

How one rule relates to the policy mode (#36).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `inherit` | Follow the effective mode. The default. |
| `always_enforce` | Enforce this rule even in audit or learning mode. |
| `never_enforce` | Never enforce this rule: it only reports what it would block. |

## EventSeverity

How serious an event is (#16).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `info` | Informational. |
| `low` | Low. |
| `medium` | Medium. |
| `high` | High. |
| `critical` | Critical. |

## Field

The identity facts a criterion can test (#31).

This is the part of the #31 catalogue that has a matcher: hashes, the
signer and its certificates, the path and the version resource. The
other families (packaged apps, installers, ownership, origin and process
relationships) arrive in later minor versions, each with its facts and
matcher.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `hash.sha256` | SHA-256 of the whole file. The primary identity (ADR 0008). |
| `hash.sha384` | SHA-384 of the whole file. |
| `hash.sha512` | SHA-512 of the whole file. |
| `hash.authenticode_sha256` | SHA-256 Authenticode image hash: the PE image without its checksum, security directory entry and certificate table. |
| `hash.authenticode_sha1` | SHA-1 Authenticode image hash. Compatibility only (ADR 0008). |
| `hash.page_sha256` | SHA-256 hash of the first page of the image, for OS-native policy formats. It covers only that page, so it is a weak identity alone. |
| `hash.page_sha1` | SHA-1 hash of the first page of the image. Compatibility only (ADR 0008). |
| `hash.msi_fuzzy_sha256` | SHA-256 of an installer package with its timestamps left out, so rebuilds of the same content share one value (#3). |
| `hash.sha1` | SHA-1 of the whole file. Compatibility only (ADR 0008). |
| `hash.md5` | MD5 of the whole file. Compatibility only (ADR 0008). |
| `signer.publisher` | The leaf signer's subject common name. |
| `signer.issuer` | The common name of the leaf certificate's issuer. |
| `signer.leaf_thumbprint` | The SHA-256 thumbprint of the leaf certificate. |
| `path.full` | The normalised full path. |
| `path.directory` | The parent directory. |
| `path.file_name` | The on-disk file name. |
| `path.extension` | The file extension, without its leading dot. |
| `meta.original_filename` | The original file name from the version resource. |
| `meta.internal_name` | The internal name from the version resource. |
| `meta.file_description` | The file description from the version resource. |
| `meta.product_name` | The product name from the version resource. |
| `meta.company_name` | The company name from the version resource. |
| `meta.file_version` | The file version from the version resource. |
| `meta.product_version` | The product version from the version resource. |
| `user.sid` | Context (#33): the SID of the user the process runs as. |
| `user.name` | Context (#33): the user's account name, as `DOMAIN\user` or as a user principal name (`user@example.org`). Either form can match. Regular expressions are not allowed: match principals by SID where you can (#32). |
| `user.groups` | Context (#33): the groups in the user's token, as SIDs, and the user's cloud-directory groups, as object IDs. |
| `user.primary_group` | Context (#33): the SID of the user's primary group. |
| `user.is_admin` | Context (#33): the token holds the local Administrators group, enabled or filtered by UAC. |
| `user.is_elevated` | Context (#33): the token is elevated. |
| `user.is_service_account` | Context (#33): the user is a service account. |
| `user.is_system` | Context (#33): the user is the local system account. |
| `device.hostname` | Context (#33): the device's host name. |
| `device.fqdn` | Context (#33): the device's fully qualified domain name. |
| `device.domain` | Context (#33): the DNS name of the device's domain. |
| `device.netbios` | Context (#33): the device's NetBIOS name. |
| `device.ad_site` | Context (#33): the directory site the device is in. |
| `device.groups` | Context (#33): the device's computer groups, as SIDs, and its cloud-directory device groups, as object IDs. |
| `device.tags` | Context (#33): the Palisade tags assigned to the device. |
| `device.os_version` | Context (#33): the operating system version. |
| `device.os_edition` | Context (#33): the operating system edition. |
| `device.arch` | Context (#33): the processor architecture, such as `x64` or `arm64`. |
| `device.is_server` | Context (#33): the device runs a server edition. |
| `device.is_domain_controller` | Context (#33): the device is a domain controller. |
| `device.is_laptop` | Context (#33): the device is a laptop. |
| `device.is_vdi` | Context (#33): the device is a virtual desktop. |
| `device.is_terminal_server` | Context (#33): the device is a multi-session terminal server. |
| `session.type` | Context (#33): how the session was started: `console`, `rdp`, `remote_shell`, `service`, `batch` or `network`. |
| `session.client_hostname` | Context (#33): the host name of the client connected to the session, on a multi-session host. |
| `session.is_remote` | Context (#33): the session is remote. |
| `user.integrity_level` | Context (#33): the integrity level of the process token: `untrusted`, `low`, `medium`, `medium_plus`, `high`, `system` or `protected`. Ordered, so `ge` and `le` compare levels. |
| `user.ou` | Context (#33): the organisational unit of the user's directory object, as a distinguished name such as `OU=Finance,DC=corp,DC=example`. With `include_sub_ous`, units below it match too. |
| `device.ou` | Context (#33): the organisational unit of the device's directory object, as for `user.ou`. |
| `device.os_build` | Context (#33): the operating system build number, such as `22631`. |
| `session.id` | Context (#33): the session ID. |
| `session.client_ip` | Context (#33): the IP address of the client connected to the session, on a multi-session host. |
| `net.ip` | Context (#33): every local interface address. A network test (`ip_in_cidr`, `ip_between`, `ip_wildcard`) matches if any address does; a set test holds the addresses as a set, so `all_of` needs every listed address to be present. |
| `net.mac` | Context (#33): every local interface MAC address. |
| `net.dns_suffix` | Context (#33): every connection-specific DNS suffix. |
| `net.connected_to_server` | Context (#33): the device can reach its server now. |
| `net.location` | Context (#33, #38): the names of the network locations the device is in, such as `corporate`, `remote` or `offline`. |
| `time.weekday` | Context (#33): the day of the week of the evaluation, as `mon` to `sun`, in the clock the policy's `time_zone_basis` names. |
| `time.local_time` | Context (#33): the time of day of the evaluation, as `HH:MM`, in the policy's clock. |
| `time.date` | Context (#33): the date of the evaluation, as `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the policy's clock. |
| `signer.leaf_thumbprint_sha1` | The SHA-1 thumbprint of the leaf certificate. Compatibility only (ADR 0008). |
| `signer.pca` | The subject common name of the highest certificate below the root, as the signature provides it: the PCA. |
| `signer.root_thumbprint` | The SHA-256 thumbprint of the chain's root certificate. |
| `signer.root_thumbprint_sha1` | The SHA-1 thumbprint of the chain's root certificate. Compatibility only (ADR 0008). |
| `signer.tbs_hash` | The hash of a chain certificate's `tbsCertificate`, under the certificate's own signature digest (40, 64, 96 or 128 hex digits). It identifies that one certificate: the `tbsCertificate` includes the serial number and the validity period (RFC 5280), so a certificate reissued with the same key has another TBS hash, and each issue needs its own rule; `signer.spki_sha256` names the key across every certificate that carries it. `signer.position` says which certificate. A 40-digit (SHA-1) value is compatibility only (ADR 0008). |
| `signer.eku` | The extended key usages of the leaf certificate, as dotted OIDs, such as `1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3` (code signing). A leaf without the extension has none. |
| `signer.spki_sha256` | The SHA-256 of a chain certificate's DER `SubjectPublicKeyInfo`: its public key (#318). Unlike the TBS hash it stays the same when a certificate is reissued for the same key, so a deny on a stolen key's hash also blocks every reissue. `signer.position` says which certificate. A key above the leaf belongs to a certificate authority, which vouches for everything it signs. |
| `meta.legal_copyright` | The `LegalCopyright` string from the version resource (#328). |
| `meta.language` | The language and code page of the version-resource block the other `meta.*` strings were read from, as its key is written: eight hex digits, such as `040904b0` (#328). |
| `meta.file_name_fallback` | The file's effective name (#328): the first of the original file name, internal name, file description and product name that the version resource has, or the name on disk when it has none. |
| `meta.file_size` | The file's size in bytes, as a whole number (#328). |
| `meta.pe_machine` | The PE image's COFF machine, by name: `i386`, `amd64`, `arm64`, `arm64_ec`, `arm64_x`, `arm_nt` and so on (#328). |
| `meta.pe_subsystem` | The PE image's subsystem, by name: `windows_gui`, `windows_cui`, `native`, `efi_application` and so on (#328). |
| `meta.is_dotnet` | Whether the PE image is a .NET assembly: it has a CLR runtime header (#328). |
| `msi.product_code` | A Windows Installer package's `ProductCode` (#328), a GUID. Compared as a GUID: braces and case do not matter. |
| `msi.upgrade_code` | A Windows Installer package's `UpgradeCode` (#328), a GUID shared by every version of a product. |
| `msi.product_name` | A Windows Installer package's `ProductName` (#328). Free text the author chooses. |
| `msi.manufacturer` | A Windows Installer package's `Manufacturer` (#328). Free text the author chooses: never a publisher. |
| `msi.product_version` | A Windows Installer package's `ProductVersion` (#328). |
| `msi.package_code` | A Windows Installer package's `PackageCode` (#328): the GUID of one build of the package. |
| `path.drive_type` | The drive type of the file's volume, as the OS reports it (#328): `fixed`, `removable`, `network`, `cd_rom` or `ram_disk`. An `unknown` drive type is a missing fact. |
| `path.bus` | The bus of the disk the file's volume is on (#328): `usb`, `sata`, `nvme`, `scsi`, `sd`, `virtual`, `file_backed_virtual`, `iscsi` and so on. An `unknown` bus is a missing fact. |
| `path.is_unc` | Whether the file is on a network share: its path, or the other form of it (a mapped drive's UNC path), is a UNC path (#328). |
| `path.is_ads` | Whether the object is an alternate data stream of a file (#328). |
| `path.share` | The `\\server\share` a file on a network share is under (#328), from its UNC path. A file on no share has none, so `equals` does not match it. |
| `path.user_can_change_acl` | Whether some non-administrator may change the permissions or the owner of the file or a directory above it (#328). |
| `meta.detected_type` | What the file's content is, from its bytes (#30, #328): `pe`, `msi`, `script`, `zip`, `lnk`, `text` and so on, in `palisade-fileid`'s names. `unknown` is a missing fact. |
| `meta.extension_type` | What the file's name claims it is, from its extension (#30, #328): one of the `Self::MetaDetectedType` names, or `none` (no extension), `inert` (a document or media extension) or `other`. A PE renamed to `.pdf` has `meta.detected_type` `pe` and `meta.extension_type` `inert`. |

## FindingSeverity

How serious a policy-assistant finding is (#40).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `info` | Informational. |
| `warning` | Probably a mistake or a risk. |
| `error` | Blocks publishing unless a tenant administrator overrides it. |

## Level

How an unknown object is handled. The variants are declared from least
to most restrictive, so `Ord` is the restrictiveness order.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `allow` | Allowed silently. Validation warns, and Essential Eight presets do not permit it for user profiles or temporary folders. |
| `detect` | Allowed, but logged with severity medium and flagged unhandled. |
| `prompt` | The user is asked (#11). Not for libraries, drivers, objects that a blocklist matched, or sessions with no interactive user; those get the prompt's fallback. |
| `restrict` | Allowed inside the `restrict_profile` containment profile (#14). Only for executables, scripts and installers. It fails closed to `block` when the containment component is not installed. |
| `block` | Blocked. The default. |

## LibraryId

A UUID version 7 in canonical lowercase form.

Type: string; matches `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-7[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`.

## LogLevel

Whether a decision produces a local event.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `always` | Every decision produces an event. |
| `summary` | Decisions are aggregated into periodic summaries per device, user, object and rule. The default for allow rules. |
| `sampled` | A sample of decisions produces events. |
| `never` | No event. |

## Mode

How a policy's decisions take effect (#36).

The variants are declared from weakest to strongest, so the derived
ordering ranks them. The "strictest" merge in #36 treats `learning` and
`audit` as equally strong; that rule belongs to the merge code, not to this
ordering.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `disabled` | The engine is not consulted. The device is reported as unprotected. |
| `monitor` | Evaluate fully, allow everything, and report would-block decisions. |
| `audit` | Like `monitor`, with a full event for every decision. |
| `learning` | Audit, and report every would-block object as a learning candidate. |
| `enforce` | Decisions take effect: blocked means blocked. |

## Notify

Whether the user is shown a notification (#11).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `none` | No notification. |
| `default` | The policy's default notification. |
| `custom` | The rule's `notification_text`. |

## ObjectType

The class of object being evaluated. Scripts are `script.<kind>`.

Values: `executable`, `library`, `driver`, `script.powershell`, `script.batch`, `script.cmd`, `script.vbscript`, `script.jscript`, `script.wsf`, `script.wsc`, `script.python`, `script.java`, `script.reg`, `script.other`, `installer`, `compiled_html`, `html_application`, `control_panel_applet`, `packaged_app`, `command`, `com_object`.

## OnWindowClose

What happens to processes a scheduled allow let run, when its schedule
closes. The engine sends a directive; the agent and the tray act on it
(#4, #11).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `none` | Nothing: they keep running. The default. |
| `warn` | Warn the user. |
| `warn_then_terminate` | Warn the user, then terminate them after the grace period. |

## Operator

How a criterion compares the fact with its values (#32). Positive
operators match if any value matches; negative operators (`not_*`)
match if no value does, and never match a fact that is unknown.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `equals` | Equal to any value. |
| `not_equals` | Equal to none of the values. |
| `starts_with` | Starts with any value. On paths, the value must end at a component boundary: `C:\Tools` does not match `C:\ToolsX`. |
| `ends_with` | Ends with any value. |
| `contains` | Contains any value. |
| `not_contains` | Contains none of the values. |
| `wildcard` | Matches any wildcard pattern. |
| `not_wildcard` | Matches none of the wildcard patterns. |
| `regex` | Matches any regular expression. Anchored at both ends, and run by a linear-time engine without look-around or backreferences. |
| `not_regex` | Matches none of the regular expressions. |
| `version_eq` | Version equal to any value. |
| `version_gt` | Version greater than the value. |
| `version_ge` | Version greater than or equal to the value. |
| `version_lt` | Version less than the value. |
| `version_le` | Version less than or equal to the value. |
| `version_between` | Version within `[min, max]`, both inclusive. Takes exactly two values, the minimum first. |
| `member_of` | The set holds any of the values (#33). |
| `not_member_of` | The set holds none of the values (#33). |
| `is_true` | The fact is true. Takes no values (#33). |
| `is_false` | The fact is false. Takes no values (#33). On an unknown fact it is unknown, like every other test. |
| `eq` | Number, level or date equal to any value (#32). |
| `ne` | Number, level or date equal to none of the values (#32). |
| `gt` | Greater than the value (#32). |
| `ge` | Greater than or equal to the value (#32). |
| `lt` | Less than the value (#32). |
| `le` | Less than or equal to the value (#32). |
| `between` | Within `[min, max]`, both inclusive. Takes exactly two values, the minimum first (#32). |
| `ip_in_cidr` | The address is in any of the CIDR blocks, such as `10.0.0.0/8` or `2001:db8::/32` (#32). On a set of addresses, any address may be. |
| `ip_between` | The address is in any of the ranges, written `first-last` or, for IPv4, `a.b.c.first-last` (#32). |
| `ip_wildcard` | The IPv4 address matches any whole-octet pattern, such as `10.*.*.*` (#32). |
| `any_of` | The set holds at least one of the values (#32). The same test as `member_of`. |
| `all_of` | The set holds every one of the values (#32). |
| `weekday_in` | The day of the week is any of the values, `mon` to `sun` (#32). |
| `time_between` | The time of day is within `[start, end)`, both `HH:MM`. A window whose end is before its start wraps midnight: `22:00` to `06:00` (#32). |
| `date_between` | The date is within `[from, to]`, both `YYYY-MM-DD` and inclusive (#32). |

## Os

The operating system a rule set targets. Other systems are reserved and
will be added in a minor version.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `windows` | Windows. |

## Pin

`latest` (the newest version) or one version number.

Type: constant or integer.

## PolicyId

The stable ID of a policy.

Type: [`Uuid7`](types.md#uuid7).

## PrecedenceModel

How the matching rules of the ordinary rule sets are combined (#35).

The mandatory-deny tier and the implicit deny for unmatched files apply
under every model (ADR 0004). The semantics of each model are in
`crate::precedence`.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `deny_wins` | Any matching deny blocks; otherwise any matching allow allows. The default. |
| `allow_wins` | Any matching allow allows. Not recommended for Essential Eight. |
| `specificity` | The rule with the most specific identity wins. |
| `first_match` | Rules are ordered, and the first match decides. |
| `priority` | The rule with the winning numeric priority decides. |

## PreexistingPolicy

What happens to files that were on the device when the agent was
installed (origin `preexisting`).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `treat_as_unknown` | They are unknown like any other object. |
| `local_approve` | The agent approves each one locally at install (#69). The engine then sees the approvals as rules, and treats a file without one as unknown. |
| `baseline_only` | They run only if the approved baseline (#5) allows them: at stage 6 they are blocked, whatever the levels say. The default. |

## PriorityDirection

Which `priority` number wins.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `lower_wins` | The lowest number wins. The default. |
| `higher_wins` | The highest number wins. |

## PromptOption

An answer the user may give to a prompt.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `allow_once` | Run this once. |
| `allow_always_local` | Run it, and approve its hash on this device (`crate::unknown::LocalApproval`). The approval is uploaded for review, and is temporary for objects from the internet, removable media or a network. |
| `request_approval` | Do not run it, and ask an administrator to approve it (#11). |
| `block` | Do not run it. |

## Reauth

What the user must do before an answer counts. Ordered from the
weakest to the strongest.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `none` | Nothing more. |
| `password` | Enter their password again. |
| `mfa` | Complete multi-factor authentication. |

## RequestTemplateRef

The ID of an approval request template (#11).

Type: [`Uuid7`](types.md#uuid7).

## RiskRating

The risk an exception carries.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `low` | Low. |
| `medium` | Medium. |
| `high` | High. |

## RuleId

The stable ID of a rule. It is never reused, even after the rule is deleted.

Type: [`Uuid7`](types.md#uuid7).

## RuleSetId

The stable ID of a rule set.

Type: [`Uuid7`](types.md#uuid7).

## RuleSetKind

The purpose of a rule set.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `allowlist` | Rules that allow. |
| `blocklist` | Rules that deny. |
| `baseline` | A baseline of what was present at a point in time. |
| `trust` | Trusted sources (#9). |
| `elevation` | Elevation rules (#12). |
| `containment` | Containment rules (#14). |
| `mixed` | Any mix of actions. |

## RuleSource

Where a rule came from.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `manual` | Written by an administrator. |
| `learned` | From learning mode (#5). |
| `recommendation` | Accepted from a recommendation (#5). |
| `catalogue` | From the curated catalogue. |
| `import` | Imported from another format. |
| `api` | Created through the API (#15). |
| `approval_request` | From an approved user request (#11). |

## SchemaVersion

A semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, without pre-release or build suffixes.

Type: string; matches `^(0\|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0\|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0\|[1-9][0-9]*)$`.

Whose token a scope's `principals` is tested against.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `process_user` | The user the process runs as. The default. |
| `session_user` | The user logged on to the process's session, for example to scope a service running as SYSTEM on behalf of the interactive user. |
| `parent_process_user` | The user the parent process runs as. |

## SessionType

How a session was started.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `console` | The physical console. |
| `rdp` | A remote desktop session. |
| `remote_shell` | A remote shell, such as a remote PowerShell session. |
| `service` | A service. |
| `batch` | A batch job, such as a scheduled task. |
| `network` | A network logon. |

## SignerSource

Where the signatures a signer criterion looks at come from (#31).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `embedded` | Embedded in the file. |
| `catalog` | A signed catalog that lists the file's hash. |
| `any` | Either. |

## SignerStatus

The result of verifying one signature (#31, #48). An unsigned object
has no `SignerFact` at all.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `valid` | The signature and chain verify, and the certificate is in date. |
| `valid_expired_timestamped` | The certificate has expired, but a trusted timestamp shows that the signature was made while it was valid. |
| `catalog_signed` | The signature verifies through a signed catalog. |
| `expired` | The certificate has expired, with no trusted timestamp. |
| `revoked` | The certificate has been revoked. |
| `untrusted_root` | The chain ends at a root that is not trusted. |
| `digest_mismatch` | The file's content does not match the signed digest. |

## SubjectComponent

The part of the leaf certificate's subject that `signer.publisher`
compares (#31).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `cn` | The common name. |
| `o` | The organisation. |
| `full_dn` | The whole distinguished name, as RFC 4514 writes it. |

## TbsPosition

Where the certificate of a `signer.tbs_hash` or `signer.spki_sha256`
test must be (#31, #318).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `leaf` | The leaf: the certificate that signed. |
| `intermediate` | Any certificate between the leaf and the root. |
| `root` | The root of the chain. |
| `any` | Anywhere in the chain. |

## TierTiebreak

Which action wins between rules of the same specificity.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `deny` | A deny beats an allow. The default. |
| `allow` | An allow beats a deny. |

## TimeOfDay

A wall-clock time, `HH:MM`, from 00:00 to 24:00.

Type: string; matches `^(([01][0-9]\|2[0-3]):[0-5][0-9]\|24:00)$`.

## TimeZoneBasis

The clock that schedules are interpreted in.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `device_local` | The device's local time zone. |
| `utc` | Coordinated Universal Time. |
| `user_local` | The time zone of the session's user, if the agent can read it, and otherwise the device's (#38). |

## Timestamp

An RFC 3339 date-time, such as `2026-11-25T09:30:00Z`. Read as UTC; fractions of a second are dropped.

Type: string; format `date-time`.

## TokenProfileRef

The ID of an access token profile for elevation (#12, #150).

Type: [`Uuid7`](types.md#uuid7).

## TrustMode

How far trust from a `trust_source` action reaches (#114).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `direct` | Only files the designated process writes itself. |
| `chained` | Files the designated process and all its descendants write. |

## UnknownAs

How a deny rule treats a result it cannot decide (#32, #35).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `no_match` | The rule does not apply. The default. |
| `match` | The rule applies, so the deny blocks. |

## Upload

When an event is sent to the server.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `immediate` | As soon as possible. |
| `batched` | With the next batch. |
| `local_only` | Never: kept in the local log only. |

## UtcDate

An RFC 3339 full date, such as `2026-11-25`, in UTC.

Type: string; format `date`.

## Uuid7

A UUID version 7 in canonical lowercase form.

Type: string; matches `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-7[0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`.

## Weekday

A day of the week.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `mon` | Monday. |
| `tue` | Tuesday. |
| `wed` | Wednesday. |
| `thu` | Thursday. |
| `fri` | Friday. |
| `sat` | Saturday. |
| `sun` | Sunday. |

## WellKnown

A well-known account or group, with a fixed SID.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `everyone` | `S-1-1-0`. |
| `authenticated_users` | `S-1-5-11`. |
| `administrators` | The local Administrators group, `S-1-5-32-544`. |
| `users` | The local Users group, `S-1-5-32-545`. |
| `system` | The local system account, `S-1-5-18`. |
| `local_service` | `S-1-5-19`. |
| `network_service` | `S-1-5-20`. |
| `interactive` | Interactive logons, `S-1-5-4`. |
| `remote_desktop_users` | `S-1-5-32-555`. |
| `domain_controllers` | Any domain's Domain Controllers group (relative ID 516), or the Enterprise Domain Controllers group, `S-1-5-9`. |
